$comment: Linter families. A family describes what stays the same across its versions; the version is chosen per run (family@version) and installed into tools/<family>@<version>/ by `pnpm arena tool add`. Fields: package: the npm package installed; with: companion packages pinned at one exact version for every version of the family (ESLint needs a TypeScript parser to read .ts files); versions: the major versions this family covers; binary: per <platform>-<arch>, or '*' for every platform, the package holding the executable and its path inside that package (a missing platform means no build is published for it); runtime: 'node' when the executable is a JavaScript file run with the current node, otherwise it is run directly; args: the arguments that lint the target with the arena's generated config, where {config} is that config's path and {target} the folder linted; env: environment set for every invocation, where {fresh} is a new empty folder made before each one (Deno keeps an incremental lint cache in DENO_DIR, so every run starts cold); threads: thread flags as documented by the linter, {n} replaced, or null when it documents none; defaultThreads: what it uses with no thread flag, as documented: a number or 'per-core'; keep: how many versions the store keeps, newest first (default 3); about: who maintains it, its repository, what it is written in and why the arena tests it, shown in the site's Libs dialog; variants: documented opt-in modes, each {args, versions, description}, run as family@version+name; source: where the thread flags are documented.

families.name: eslint
families.description: The JavaScript linter, with the typescript-eslint parser for TypeScript files

about.why: The linter most projects run today and the source of most rule names. Every other linter is compared with it.

families.name: oxlint
families.description: The Oxc project's linter, written in Rust

about.language: Rust, shipped as a Node native addon
about.why: Ports ESLint's core rules and common plugins, and reads ESLint's disable comments, so it is the most direct ESLint replacement.

families.name: biome
families.description: Biome's linter (biome lint), written in Rust

about.why: A linter and formatter in one native binary, with its own rule names mapped to ESLint's by `biome migrate eslint`.

families.source: biome lint --help documents no thread option; BIOME_THREADS is documented for biome ci only

families.name: deno
families.description: Deno's built-in linter (deno lint), written in Rust

about.why: A linter built into a runtime, with ESLint's rule names for the rules it shares.

families.source: deno lint --help documents no thread option
